pluss::timeline::make¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::make(std::string_view value)
Timeline pluss::timeline::make(string_range values)
Timeline pluss::timeline::make(nested_string_values values)
Timeline pluss::timeline::make(string_range flat, integer_range sizes)

Parse Timestamp Text Into Instants¶

make() is the general text entrance to Timeline. Use it when each token may contain a complete timestamp, a date alone, or an explicit numeric UTC offset. It parses every token into one signed epoch-nanosecond tick and returns a UTC timeline with the shape implied by the selected call form.

Parsing an instant and remembering its source spelling are different jobs. make() retains the instant, not the original separator, offset spelling, or fractional width. Consequently, 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and 2023-12-31T17:00:00-07:00 become equal ticks. Use format() later to choose one consistent representation.

Choose a narrower factory when the grammar itself is part of the contract: date() rejects clock fields, while time() rejects calendar fields. An empty or whitespace-only token is the deliberate text spelling for NaT; malformed nonempty text throws.

Accepted Text¶

The documented grammar includes:

  • dates as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY/MM/DD

  • a date followed by a clock, separated by T or a space

  • HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, and fractional seconds

  • Z, +HH:MM, -HH:MM, +HHMM, or -HHMM suffixes

  • surrounding ASCII whitespace

A token without an offset is interpreted as UTC. Fractions shorter than nine digits are right-padded to nanoseconds. Digits beyond nanosecond precision are discarded rather than rounded. Calendar dates, clock fields, offsets, and the representable nanosecond range are validated before a result is returned.

Example 1: Scalar Input Produces Rank Zero¶

const auto event =
    pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T23:30:45.123456789-07:00");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(event, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-03-01T06:30:45.123456789+00:00"

The date changes because the source text describes an instant seven hours behind UTC. The result is a scalar, not a one-element vector.

Example 2: One-Dimensional Mixed Forms And NaT¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-02-29", "2024/03/01 06:15",
    "2024-03-01T08:15:00+0200", ""});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(events, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["2024-02-29T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-03-01T06:15:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-03-01T06:15:00.000000000+00:00", "NaT"]

Date-only input starts at midnight. The middle two spellings resolve to the same instant. The empty token creates absence without weakening other lanes.

Example 3: Nested Braces Infer Matrix Shape¶

const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02T03:04:05Z"},
    {"2024-01-03T06:07Z", "2024-01-04T08:09:10.5Z"},
});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(matrix, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-01-02T03:04:05.000000000+00:00"], 
  ["2024-01-03T06:07:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-01-04T08:09:10.500000000+00:00"]
]

Nested rows must be rectangular. Shape is inferred before parsing, and Timeline accepts ranks zero through three.

Example 4: Runtime Flat Storage With Explicit Geometry¶

const std::vector<std::string> flat{
    "2024-04-01", "2024-04-02", "2024-04-03", "2024-04-04"};
const auto cube = pluss::timeline::make(flat, {1, 2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(cube, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2, 2], dim=3, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  [
    ["2024-04-01T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-04-02T00:00:00.000000000+00:00"], 
    ["2024-04-03T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-04-04T00:00:00.000000000+00:00"]
  ]
]

The flat range is interpreted in row-major order. Its cardinality must equal the product of sizes; zero extents are allowed, negative extents and ranks above three are not.

Example 5: Offsets Identify Instants¶

const auto same = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2023-12-31T17:00:00-07:00"});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, same.epoch_nanos());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1704067200000000000, 1704067200000000000]

Failure Modes¶

The entire construction fails if any defined token is invalid. Representative failures include impossible dates, invalid numeric offsets, ragged nesting, shape/cardinality mismatch, and timestamps outside the signed nanosecond range.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeline::make("2023-02-29");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected
